chunks: My father (rah) said: from Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqteeni from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abi Basir from Abi Ja’far (peace be upon him) who said:
Allah takes revenge upon an unjust person through another unjust person.
And this is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic,
And thus do We make some of the iniquitous to rule upon others.

key_terms.بَعْضَ الظَّالِمِینَ بَعْضاً: some of the unjust over others

ai.seo_question: How does divine justice utilize unjust people to punish other unjust people?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq to illustrate the principle of *tadakhul* (interconnectedness) in divine justice, where God utilizes the inherent nature of the oppressor to punish them. This mechanism reflects the Quranic concept of *bi-ithmihim* (by their own sins), where the tyrant becomes the instrument of their own downfall, serving as both a practical reality in history and a spiritual lesson in self-inflicted consequence.
